chain.note: Association is genetic; direct cellular causality has not been demonstrated by any record retrieved.

object.label: endoplasmic reticulum stress in bronchiolar epithelium

chain.note: UniProt also records DSP as a negative regulator of MAPK/PI3K signalling and as raising TGFB1 abundance in cardiomyocytes; sign may be context-dependent.

subject.label: EMT and ER stress in distal airway epithelium

contradicting_evidence: HPA:ENSG00000117983 shows MUC5B is enriched in salivary gland and submucosal glandular/goblet cells, not lung, and HPA:ENSG00000096696 shows DSP is enriched in esophagus and skin basal keratinocytes — in normal lung neither gene marks the distal airspace, so the proposed cell of origin only exists in the remodelled (fibrotic) lung

STRING:SFTPC-MUC5B and the other set edges are text-mining only (experimental 0.00), and DSP has no STRING edge to any other gene in the list, so there is no physical or curated-pathway link between MUC5B and DSP
OT:MUC5B-constraint and OT:DSP-constraint show both genes are the least loss-of-function-constrained in the set (score 1, bin 0), which argues against simple haploinsufficiency mechanisms

falsification.description: In human distal airway organoids or precision-cut lung slices carrying the rs35705950 risk allele, knock down MUC5B (or block mucin secretion) and measure ER stress markers (BiP/CHOP/spliced XBP1) and EMT/YAP target gene induction in DSP-expressing epithelium. If MUC5B knockdown does not reduce ER stress and does not restore desmosomal/junctional gene programmes, the hypothesis that mucin burden is upstream of junctional/EMT change fails; equally, restoring DSP should blunt EMT if the arm is real.

readout.label: epithelial ER stress and EMT/YAP target gene expression

falsification.system: human distal airway/bronchiolar organoid genotyped at rs35705950

hypotheses.mechanism: The MUC5B promoter variant rs35705950 drives ectopic expression of a secreted gel-forming mucin in the respiratory bronchiole, where mucin biosynthesis overloads the secretory pathway and initiates ER stress in the very epithelium that lines honeycomb cysts. DSP, a desmosomal plakin whose normal expression is basal/apical stratified epithelium rather than alveolus, sits at the same GWAS-defined airway-epithelial axis and constrains epithelial-mesenchymal transition through Hippo/YAP; loss or dysregulation of DSP-anchored junctions in this ectopic airway epithelium permits EMT and profibrotic signalling. The two genes therefore describe one lesion — a mislocated, mucus-secreting, junctionally destabilised distal airway epithelium — not two independent risk loci. This predicts that the fibrotic driver is airway-epithelial secretory burden, not alveolar loss per se.
hypotheses.title: Distal airway secretory reprogramming: MUC5B over-expression plus DSP-dependent junction/EMT change converts the respiratory bronchiole into a fibrogenic, ER-stressed epithelium

chain.note: Reactome curates a defective pro-SFTPC disease pathway; the causal step to fibrosis specifically is not demonstrated in any retrieved primary record.

contradicting_evidence: HPA:ENSG00000164362 records TERT as not detected in normal human tissues including lung, so the cell in which telomerase loss acts cannot be demonstrated by expression data — the mechanism is inferred from genetics and telomere length, not from measured TERT in AT2 cells

The literature specialist found no primary record demonstrating that an SFTPC mutation causes AT2 unfolded-protein-response activation that drives fibrosis, nor AT2-specific senescence from TERT mutation; both arms are review- rather than experiment-supported here

falsification.description: Delete Tert conditionally in AT2 cells (Sftpc-CreER) in mice already carrying a BRICHOS-mutant Sftpc allele and compare with each single perturbation after a low-dose injury. If AT2 senescence markers, KRT8+ transitional-state persistence and fibrosis are no greater than with either lesion alone, the claim that telomere attrition and pro-SFTPC misfolding converge on one AT2 proteostasis/renewal bottleneck is falsified.

readout.label: AT2 senescence and persistent KRT8+ transitional state

falsification.system: AT2-conditional mouse model with low-dose injury

hypotheses.mechanism: AT2 cells are the alveolar progenitor and the only cell in this list with an unambiguous lung identity (SFTPC is essentially AT2-exclusive). Rare TERT loss-of-function alleles shorten telomeres and remove the replicative reserve that AT2 cells need to re-epithelialise after injury, while BRICHOS-domain pro-SFTPC mutants overload AT2 proteostasis; both funnel into AT2 senescence/apoptosis, a persistent KRT8+/KRT17+ transitional state, and failure of alveolar regeneration. Reactome independently recovers 'Surfactant metabolism' and 'Defective pro-SFTPC causes SMDP2 and RDS' as the only coherent block in the set, and TERT as the senescence/DNA-damage arm — two failure modes of one cell, not two diseases.
hypotheses.title: Alveolar type II cell exhaustion: TERT-dependent telomere attrition and misfolded pro-SFTPC converge on the same AT2 proteostasis/senescence failure

chain.note: PANTHER showed no benefit of NAC in the unselected population; the hypothesis is that benefit is confined to a TOLLIP genotype stratum, which this record does not itself establish.

contradicting_evidence: R-HSA-5683826 and the rest of the Reactome result: no TOLLIP-driven TLR/IL-1 pathway reached significance in this gene set, so the innate-immune arm is not recovered by set-level enrichment

The trials specialist could not retrieve any TOLLIP-genotype-stratified N-acetylcysteine registration (e.g. PRECISIONS), so the pharmacogenetic claim rests on the PANTHER trial record plus the mortality GWAS, not on a prospective stratified trial
HPA:ENSG00000078902 shows TOLLIP has low tissue specificity with no lung enrichment, giving no cell-type anchor for the mechanism

falsification.description: Prospectively randomise IPF patients stratified by TOLLIP rs3750920/rs5743890 genotype to N-acetylcysteine versus placebo with FVC decline and mortality as endpoints, and in parallel knock down TOLLIP in primary human lung epithelial cells and measure IRAK1 phosphorylation, IL-1-driven cytokine output and autophagic clearance of ubiquitin conjugates. If genotype does not modify treatment effect and TOLLIP knockdown does not disinhibit IL-1R/TLR output in lung epithelium, the hypothesis fails.

readout.label: IRAK1 phosphorylation and IL-1-driven cytokine output

falsification.system: primary human lung epithelial cells; genotype-stratified IPF trial

hypotheses.mechanism: TOLLIP is a cytoplasmic/early-endosomal adapter that recruits IRAK1 to the IL-1R complex and inhibits its phosphorylation, and that couples ubiquitin conjugates to ATG8 proteins for selective autophagy. Reduced TOLLIP function would therefore both disinhibit innate immune signalling after repeated micro-injury and impair clearance of the ubiquitinated protein aggregates generated by the ER-stressed epithelium of H1/H2. This predicts that TOLLIP genotype should modulate disease *course* and drug response rather than simply risk — consistent with the same GWAS reporting TOLLIP variants associated with mortality, and with the pharmacogenetic interaction between TOLLIP genotype and N-acetylcysteine in the PANTHER trial population.
hypotheses.title: Host-response set point: TOLLIP-dependent restraint of IL-1R/TLR signalling and ubiquitin-directed autophagy sets injury response and treatment response, not baseline susceptibility

chain.note: Inferred from the Rho-GAP domain and a review; UniProt has no curated function statement and no primary experiment was retrieved.
Shared association across fibrotic and emphysematous lung phenotypes is the main argument for a modifier rather than an initiator role.

object.label: UIP pattern in systemic sclerosis ILD and in emphysema/CPFE

contradicting_evidence: O94988: UniProt records no curated function and no subcellular location for FAM13A, so the Rho-GAP mechanism is a domain inference, not an annotation
HPA:ENSG00000138640 shows no lung enrichment (top cell types adipocytes, pancreatic acinar, pituicytes), giving no lung cell-type anchor
STRING returns only text-mining edges from FAM13A to MUC5B (0.51) and TOLLIP (0.40) with experimental scores ~0, so FAM13A is not part of any physical module with the rest of the list

falsification.description: Knock out FAM13A, and separately express a GAP-dead point mutant, in primary human lung fibroblasts and alveolar epithelial cells, then measure RhoA-GTP loading, actomyosin contraction/traction force, beta-catenin target gene expression and TGF-beta-induced myofibroblast differentiation. If loss of FAM13A and the GAP-dead mutant produce no change in RhoA activity or contractile/Wnt output, the Rho-GAP modifier hypothesis is dead and FAM13A must be acting through a non-catalytic route.

readout.label: RhoA-GTP loading and myofibroblast contractile differentiation

falsification.system: primary human lung fibroblasts and alveolar epithelial cells

hypotheses.mechanism: FAM13A carries a Rho-GAP domain but has no curated UniProt function statement and no lung-enriched expression; it is nonetheless one of the most reproducibly replicated IPF GWAS loci and is shared with COPD/emphysema and with a UIP pattern in systemic sclerosis ILD. The parsimonious reading is that FAM13A acts as a RhoA-directed modifier of cytoskeletal tension and Wnt/beta-catenin signalling in mesenchymal and epithelial cells, setting the amplitude of the fibrotic or emphysematous response to injury rather than initiating it — which is why the same locus produces opposite-looking lung phenotypes depending on the co-occurring epithelial lesion. Its Open Targets safety liability (body mass index) and degrader-only tractability are consistent with a broadly acting cytoskeletal regulator.
hypotheses.title: FAM13A is a Rho-GAP modifier of mesenchymal/epithelial mechanotransduction shared between emphysema and fibrosis, and is not part of the epithelial secretory or telomere modules

chain.note: The only set-level enrichment is co-citation and the disease term itself.

subject.label: MUC5B, TERT, SFTPC, TOLLIP, DSP, FAM13A

object.label: failed repair of repetitive distal lung injury

subject.label: independent epithelial lesions (secretion, junctions, proteostasis, replicative reserve, immune set point, tension)

contradicting_evidence: P15924 records that DSP binds telomeric DNA via its C-terminus and maintains telomere length through TRF2, which would place DSP and TERT in a shared telomere module; STRING found no DSP edge to TERT, TERF2, TERF1, TINF2, POT1 or RTEL1, so the two sources disagree on whether a DSP-telomere axis exists
Open Targets gives every gene a substantial genetic_association component (TERT 0.87 down to TOLLIP 0.59), so the set is not merely a text-mining artefact even though its internal edges are

falsification.description: Test for statistical interaction (epistasis) between rs35705950 and the TERT, DSP, TOLLIP and FAM13A risk alleles in a large IPF case-control cohort, and in parallel test whether a single pathway intervention (e.g. IRE1alpha inhibition) normalises fibrotic outcome regardless of which risk allele a patient-derived organoid carries. Significant epistasis, or uniform rescue across genotypes, would falsify the convergence-without-interaction claim and re-establish the set as one module.
falsification.system: IPF case-control cohort; patient-derived distal lung organoids

hypotheses.mechanism: STRING finds no experimentally supported edge anywhere in the set — every edge is text-mining with experimental and database scores of ~0.00, DSP has no edge at all, and the only enrichments are the DISEASES term 'idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis' and co-citation in the same GWAS papers. Reactome likewise returns only single-gene hits (surfactant metabolism for SFTPC, MITF-M/senescence for TERT, apoptotic cleavage of adhesion proteins for DSP) with nothing joining them. The correct causal statement is therefore convergence, not interaction: independent lesions in mucociliary secretion (MUC5B), junction integrity (DSP), progenitor replicative capacity (TERT), surfactant proteostasis (SFTPC), innate-immune set point (TOLLIP) and cytoskeletal tension (FAM13A) each raise the probability that repetitive distal-lung injury resolves as fibrosis rather than repair. This predicts additive, not epistatic, genetic risk and argues for patient stratification by which arm is broken rather than one common target.
hypotheses.title: The set is not a module: these six genes are a literature-defined risk list whose only shared node is the injured distal lung epithelium, so no single pathway intervention will address them
